description: Every paragraph, clause, heading, definition, signature block, and footnote in the English source NDA has a corresponding Spanish translation in the deliverable, with no content omitted or added.
verification: Align source and target segments; pass if every source segment maps to a translated target segment and no target segment lacks a source counterpart. Untranslated English text left in the body (other than proper names) fails.

description: All numbers, amounts, durations, dates, party names, addresses, and cross-references in the source appear unchanged in meaning in the Spanish text.
verification: Extract numerals, dates, durations (e.g., 'two (2) years'), monetary amounts, party/company names, and clause cross-references from source and target; pass only if every item matches. Date formats may be localized but must denote the same date.

description: The Spanish document keeps the source's section and subsection numbering identically, in the same order and hierarchy.
verification: Extract the numbering sequence (e.g., 1, 1.1, 1.2, 2, (a), (b)) from both documents; pass if the sequences are identical.

description: Every occurrence of 'Confidential Information' is translated as 'Información Confidencial', preserving the source's capitalization as a defined term.
verification: Count occurrences of 'Confidential Information' in the source and 'Información Confidencial' in the target; pass if every source occurrence corresponds to 'Información Confidencial' and no alternative rendering (e.g., 'información confidencial' in lowercase or 'Información Reservada') replaces a source defined-term occurrence.

description: The translation conveys the same legal obligations, rights, exceptions, and conditions as the source without mistranslations that change meaning.
verification: Run translation quality estimation on aligned segments, then have a judge review flagged segments. Fail if any clause changes who owes an obligation, its scope, an exception, a condition, or a permission/prohibition (e.g., 'shall' rendered as optional, 'mutual' obligations made one-sided).

description: The text is in formal legal Spanish appropriate for Mexico, with no slang, no informal 'tú' address, and no Spain-specific forms such as 'vosotros'.
verification: Search for 'tú'/'vosotros' verb forms and pronouns and informal expressions; a judge confirms that the terminology reads as standard Mexican contractual Spanish (e.g., 'contrato', 'las partes', 'obligaciones'). Pass if none found and the judge confirms the formal legal register.

description: The deliverable is a valid .docx file that opens without errors.
verification: Check the file extension is .docx and the file parses as valid Office Open XML (e.g., opens with python-docx).

description: The .docx preserves the source's structural formatting: headings, paragraph breaks, lists, bold/underlined defined terms, and signature block layout.
verification: Compare the source and target document structure; pass if the counts of headings, list items, and signature blocks match and defined terms that are emphasized in the source remain emphasized in the target.

description: Every source segment (headings, paragraphs, list items, table cells, footnotes) has a corresponding French translation, with no untranslated English passages left in running text.
verification: Align source and target at segment level. Fail if any source segment has no target counterpart or if any target segment is still in English, excluding proper names, product names, URLs and email addresses.

description: The translation adds no content (sentences, clauses, obligations, rights or disclaimers) that is absent from the source.
verification: Segment alignment plus a bilingual review flags any target segment, or any substantive clause within a segment, that has no basis in the source. Fail if any is found.

description: Every legal obligation, right, permission, condition, time period and party in the source keeps the same meaning in French, with no reversals, omissions or changes in scope (for example 'may' becoming 'must', or 'we do not sell' becoming 'we sell').
verification: A bilingual quality-estimation check plus a judge comparison of each aligned segment. Fail on any segment where a right, obligation, condition, modal force, negation or data-use scope differs from the source.

description: All numbers, dates, durations, monetary amounts, percentages, company and product names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses and URLs from the source appear unchanged in value in the translation.
verification: Extract these entities from source and target and compare them. Numeric format may follow French-Canadian conventions (e.g. '1 000', '25 $', '30 jours'), but values must match exactly. Email addresses, URLs and phone numbers must match character for character. Fail on any mismatch or omission.

description: The translation uses Canadian French (fr-CA) vocabulary and conventions rather than France French.
verification: Judge checks for fr-CA terminology and flags France-specific usage, for example 'mail'/'e-mail'/'mél' instead of 'courriel', or 'portable' instead of 'cellulaire' where a phone is meant. Fail if France-specific terms appear where a standard Canadian French equivalent exists.

description: References to Canadian laws, regulators and legal concepts use their official Canadian French names, for example PIPEDA as 'Loi sur la protection des renseignements personnels et les documents électroniques (LPRPDE)' and 'personal information' as 'renseignements personnels'.
verification: For every Canadian statute, regulator or defined legal concept named in the source, check the target against its official French name as published by the Government of Canada or Québec. Fail on any non-official rendering, such as 'données personnelles' used for the PIPEDA term 'personal information'.

description: The translation addresses the reader formally throughout.
verification: Search the target for 'tu', 'te', 't'', 'ton', 'ta', 'tes' and 'toi' used as second-person address. Fail if any instance addresses the reader.

description: The translation keeps the source's structure: the same number and order of headings, sections, numbered or bulleted lists, tables and links.
verification: Compare the counts and order of headings, list items, tables and hyperlinks between source and target. Fail on any difference in count or order.

description: Each recurring defined term or key concept in the source, such as the company's defined name, 'personal information', 'cookies' and 'third parties', is translated the same way every time it appears.
verification: List the recurring terms in the source and collect their French renderings across the target. Fail if any term has more than one rendering without a clear grammatical reason.

description: Every clause, paragraph, table, annex, footnote and signature block in the German source has a corresponding English translation, with no source segments omitted.
verification: Align source and target segments (sentence/paragraph alignment); fail if any source segment containing text has no aligned target segment or is left untranslated in German.

description: The translation contains no substantive content absent from the source, such as added clauses, explanations or legal commentary. Bracketed translator's notes are allowed only if clearly marked as translator's notes.
verification: Run segment alignment. Fail if any target segment has no source counterpart, unless it is explicitly labeled as a translator's note.

description: Every number in the source appears with the same value in the translation, including rents, deposits, areas, percentages, index values, notice periods and clause or section numbers. Currency is kept as stated (e.g., EUR stays EUR).
verification: Extract all numeric values and currency amounts from the source and the target, normalizing German decimal and thousands separators (1.234,56 → 1,234.56). Fail if any value is missing, altered or converted to another currency.

description: Every date in the source appears in the translation with the same day, month and year, written unambiguously (month spelled out or ISO format) so US readers cannot misread day/month order.
verification: Extract the dates from both texts and compare day, month and year. Fail if any date is missing or changed. Fail if any date is written in an ambiguous all-numeric DD/MM or MM/DD form.

description: All party names, company names with their legal-form suffixes (e.g., GmbH, AG, GmbH & Co. KG), personal names, addresses and register numbers (e.g., HRB) are reproduced exactly as in the source and are not translated or altered.
verification: Extract the proper names, legal-entity names, addresses and register numbers from the source. Fail if any does not appear verbatim in the target, allowing only the transliteration of umlauts and ß where applicable (ä→ae, ö→oe, ü→ue, ß→ss).

description: The obligations, rights, conditions, deadlines and legal terms in each clause are rendered with the same meaning as the source. German legal terms of art without an exact US equivalent (e.g., Nebenkosten, Schriftform, Kündigung) are translated consistently, and the original German term appears in parentheses at first use.
verification: Run translation quality estimation on each segment. A judge then reviews flagged and key clauses (rent, term, termination, deposit, liability, operating costs) and fails the criterion if any clause's legal meaning is changed, reversed or omitted, if a German term of art lacks its parenthetical German original at first use, or if a term of art is translated inconsistently.

description: The translation is written in English, using US spelling conventions.
verification: Run language identification on the target, then spot-check spellings (e.g., -ize/-or forms). Fail if any non-English running text remains, other than names or quoted German terms, or if British spellings predominate.

description: The translation keeps the source's section and clause numbering, headings, ordering, and table layout so that clauses can be cross-referenced against the German original.
verification: Compare the sequence of section and clause identifiers (e.g., §1, §2.1, Annex 1) and the table count in source and target. Fail if any are missing, renumbered or reordered.

description: The deliverable is a single valid UTF-8 JSON file with the same nesting structure as the English source file.
verification: Parse the deliverable with a strict JSON parser and confirm it decodes as UTF-8. Compare the tree shape (objects, arrays, nesting paths) to the source file. Pass only if parsing succeeds and every structural path matches.

description: The set of keys at every level is identical to the source: no key is renamed, added, or removed.
verification: Extract all full key paths from the source and the deliverable and compare them as sets. Pass only if the two sets are exactly equal, character for character, including case.

description: Every string value is a non-empty Portuguese translation, with no value left in English except brand names, product names, or strings that contain only placeholders or symbols.
verification: Flag every value that is empty or identical to its English source. Run language identification on the remaining values. Pass only if every flagged or non-Portuguese value is a proper noun, a brand name, or a placeholder/symbol-only string.

description: Each translated value contains exactly the same placeholders as its source value, such as {count}, {name}, %s, %d, and %1$s, with identical spelling and the same number of occurrences.
verification: For each key, extract placeholder tokens from source and target with regexes for \{[^}]+\} and printf-style %(\d+\$)?[sdif@]. Compare them as multisets. Pass only if they match for every key.

description: Any HTML/XML tags, escape sequences (e.g., \n, \t), and ICU plural/select syntax in a source value appear unchanged in its translation.
verification: For each key, extract tags (<[^>]+>), escape sequences, and ICU keywords/selectors (plural, select, one, other, =0, etc.) from source and target. Compare them as multisets. Pass only if they match for every key.

description: Every translated button label is at most 30 characters long.
verification: Identify button-label keys using the rule agreed in open questions (e.g., key path containing 'button' or 'btn'). Count Unicode characters (code points) of each translated value, with placeholders counted as written. Pass only if every button label has 30 or fewer characters.

description: Translations use Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR) vocabulary, spelling, and address forms, not European Portuguese.
verification: Scan all values for European Portuguese markers (e.g., ecrã, ficheiro, utilizador, telemóvel, 'tu' verb forms used as default address, gerund replaced by 'a + infinitive'). Have a pt-BR specialist verifier confirm the variant. Pass if no European-Portuguese-specific forms are found.

description: No translated value contains a meaning error, meaning a mistranslation, an omission, or added content that changes what the UI string tells the user.
verification: Run segment-level translation quality estimation on every source/target pair. Have a bilingual reviewer or judge check all flagged segments. Pass only if no segment is confirmed to have a major error, defined as wrong meaning, missing information, added information, or inverted action, e.g., 'Cancel' rendered as 'Confirmar'.

description: The same English UI term (e.g., 'Settings', 'Sign in', 'Delete') is translated the same way throughout the file.
verification: Align recurring English terms that appear in two or more values with their Portuguese renderings. Pass if each recurring term maps to a single Portuguese rendering, allowing grammatical inflection, or if any variation is justified by context, as confirmed by a judge.

description: The deliverable is written in German throughout, with no untranslated English sentences other than brand names, product names, and trademarks.
verification: Run language identification per segment; every segment must be detected as German, except segments consisting only of brand/product names or trademarks.

description: Every sentence, heading, bullet point and list item in the source description has a corresponding German translation, and no new claims, features or content are added.
verification: Align source and target segments. Pass if every source segment maps to a target segment and no target segment lacks a source counterpart.

description: All numbers, measurements, quantities, prices, percentages and model numbers in the source appear unchanged in value in the translation.
verification: Extract all numeric values from source and target and compare them. Pass if every source value appears in the target with the same value. Locale formatting differences are allowed, such as a decimal comma or € placement.

description: Brand names, product names, trademarks and SKUs from the source appear in the translation spelled exactly as in the source.
verification: Extract capitalized proper nouns, trademarked terms (™/®) and alphanumeric codes from the source and check that each appears verbatim in the target.

description: The translation conveys the same product features, specifications and claims as the source, with no mistranslations that change meaning.
verification: Run translation quality estimation and a bilingual judge review per segment. Fail if any segment omits, reverses or distorts a product feature, specification, material, compatibility statement or claim.

description: The translation keeps the source's structure: the same number and order of headings, paragraphs and bullet lists, and any HTML/Shopify markup tags intact.
verification: Compare counts and order of headings, paragraphs and list items between source and target. If the source contains HTML tags, they must appear in the target with identical tag structure and attributes.

description: The German reads as fluent, natural e-commerce marketing copy rather than literal word-for-word translation.
verification: A judge fluent in German reviews the text. Fail if it finds unnatural calqued phrasing, awkward word order, grammatical or spelling errors, or sentences a native German copywriter would not write. A minor stylistic preference alone is not a failure.

description: The text addresses the customer in one form of address consistently throughout, never mixing 'du' and 'Sie'.
verification: Count second-person forms ('du/dich/dir/dein' vs 'Sie/Ihnen/Ihr' as address). Pass if only one form is used.

description: Every sentence, heading, list item, and signature/footer block of the English source letter is translated into Spanish, with no source segments omitted.
verification: Segment-align source and target; fail if any source segment has no corresponding Spanish segment or is left untranslated in English (proper names, company names, and job titles left in English are allowed).

description: The translation adds no clauses, conditions, explanations, or translator notes that are absent from the source.
verification: Segment alignment flags target segments with no source counterpart; a judge confirms any flagged segment introduces new meaning. Fail if any such segment exists.

description: Every salary/compensation figure (amount, currency, and pay period such as annual, hourly, or bi-weekly) matches the source exactly.
verification: Extract all monetary amounts and their pay periods from source and target; fail on any mismatch in value, currency, or period. Locale-appropriate separators that preserve the value (e.g. $85,000.00) are allowed.

description: The start date and any other dates in the letter (offer expiry, response deadline) refer to the same calendar day as in the source.
verification: Extract dates from source and target and normalize them; fail if any date differs or is missing. The Spanish month-name format ('15 de marzo de 2025') is acceptable.

description: Every benefit in the source (e.g. health insurance, PTO days, 401(k) match percentage, bonus, equity) appears in the translation with identical quantities, percentages, eligibility periods, and conditions.
verification: List each benefit and its numeric terms from the source; confirm each has an equivalent in the target with matching numbers and conditions. Fail on any missing benefit or changed term.

description: Personal names, the company name, addresses, and contact details are reproduced exactly as in the source.
verification: Extract named entities, emails, phone numbers, and addresses from the source; string-match each one in the target. Fail on any alteration.

description: The Spanish uses US Hispanic conventions: neutral Latin American vocabulary, 'ustedes' rather than 'vosotros', and no Spain-specific terms.
verification: Scan for vosotros verb forms and pronouns and for Peninsular-only terms (e.g. 'ordenador', 'coger' meaning 'take', 'nómina' used for a US paycheck); a judge confirms no Spain-specific usage. Fail if any is found.

description: The letter addresses the candidate formally with 'usted' throughout and uses professional business register.
verification: Fail if any 'tú' forms are used to address the candidate, or if slang or colloquialisms appear.

description: Legal and employment terms (e.g. at-will employment, exempt/non-exempt status, contingencies such as background checks) are translated with their meaning intact.
verification: Run translation quality estimation on all segments; a judge reviews employment and legal clauses and fails the criterion if any clause's obligation, condition, or right is changed, weakened, or reversed.

description: The translation keeps the source layout: the same paragraphs, headings, lists, and signature/acceptance blocks, in the same order.
verification: Compare the structural elements of source and target, including paragraph count, heading count, list items, and signature lines. Fail if any is missing or reordered.

description: The German translation contains all 12 sections of the source Terms of Service, in the same order, with section numbering preserved.
verification: Count top-level sections in source and deliverable; pass if both have 12 and the section numbers/order match one-to-one.

description: Every source sentence/clause is translated and no content is added that is not in the source.
verification: Segment-align source and target; pass if every source segment has a corresponding target segment and no target segment lacks a source counterpart (excluding pure formatting).

description: The translated body text is in German, with no untranslated English passages other than proper names, product names, URLs, or terms the source itself leaves untranslated.
verification: Run language identification per segment; pass if all body segments are German, and any English-detected segment is only a proper name, URL, or brand.

description: All numbers, dates, monetary amounts, percentages, time periods, email addresses, URLs, and company/legal entity names from the source appear unchanged in value in the translation (localized number/date formatting is allowed).
verification: Extract these entities from source and target; pass if every source entity has a value-equivalent match in the target and no values differ.

description: The reader is addressed exclusively with formal 'Sie' forms (Sie, Ihnen, Ihr/Ihre capitalized), with no informal 'du/dich/dir/dein/ihr' second-person address.
verification: Search target for informal second-person pronouns and verb forms (du, dich, dir, dein*, euch, euer); pass if none are used as address to the reader and formal pronouns are capitalized.

description: Every occurrence of a defined term that is bold in the source has a corresponding bold term in the translation, and no additional text is bolded.
verification: Extract bold spans from source and target; pass if the count of bold spans matches per section and each source bold span aligns to a target bold span translating it.

description: Each defined term is translated with one consistent German rendering throughout the whole document.
verification: For each source defined term, collect its German renderings across all occurrences; pass if each term maps to a single rendering (allowing only grammatical inflection).

description: The translation preserves the legal meaning of each clause, including obligations, rights, conditions, exclusions, and negations, without reversing or weakening any provision.
verification: Judge compares aligned segments and fails if any clause changes who is obligated, inverts a negation, drops a condition/exception, or changes modal force (e.g., 'must' rendered as 'may').

description: Headings, lists, paragraph breaks, and other formatting of the source are preserved in the translation.
verification: Compare document structure (headings, list items, paragraph count per section); pass if counts match per section within ±1 paragraph and all headings and list items are present.

description: Every source segment (headings, body text, numbered steps, table cells, captions, warnings, footnotes) has a corresponding French translation, with no segments omitted and no content added.
verification: Align source and target segment by segment. Fail if any source segment has no aligned target segment, or any target segment has no source counterpart (beyond grammatically required words).

description: All translated text is in French.
verification: Run language identification on each target segment. Fail if any segment other than untranslatable items (product names, model numbers, unit symbols, standard codes) is identified as English or any language other than French.

description: Every dosage figure and other numeric value in the source appears unchanged in the corresponding target segment.
verification: Extract all numbers, including decimals, ranges, ratios and percentages, from each aligned source/target segment pair and compare them. Fail on any missing, added or altered value, including changed digits or a changed decimal position. Decimal-separator handling follows the buyer's answer to the open question; if unanswered, the separator must match the source.

description: Every unit of measure in the source (for example mg, mL, µg, IU, °C, mmHg, kg) is preserved with the same unit and attached to the same value in the target.
verification: Extract unit symbols and their associated numbers from each aligned segment pair. Fail if any unit is missing, converted, replaced by a different unit, or attached to a different value.

description: Every source warning appears as a warning in the target, carries the heading 'AVERTISSEMENT' (as specified in the open question), and is placed in the same order.
verification: Count source blocks headed 'WARNING' and target blocks headed 'AVERTISSEMENT'. Fail if the counts differ, any heading is missing or reworded, or the warnings appear in a different order.

description: Each warning's French text conveys the same hazard, condition and required or prohibited action as the source, with no softening, strengthening or omission.
verification: For each aligned warning pair, a bilingual medical-translation reviewer checks hazard, trigger condition, action and negations such as 'do not' / 'ne pas'. Fail if any of these elements is changed, dropped or inverted.

description: Instructions, contraindications and procedural steps outside the warnings are translated without errors that change the meaning, including the action, sequence, negation, frequency or patient population.
verification: Run translation quality estimation, then have a bilingual reviewer check every segment flagged below threshold plus all numbered steps and contraindications. Fail if any meaning-changing error is found.

description: Product names, model and catalogue numbers, standard references (for example ISO or EN codes) and symbols are reproduced exactly as in the source.
verification: Extract alphanumeric identifiers, trademarks and standard codes from the source and string-match them in the corresponding target segments. Fail on any absent or altered item.

description: The target keeps the source's structure: the same heading hierarchy, the same number and order of numbered or bulleted steps, the same tables with the same row and column counts, and the same file format.
verification: Compare document structure between source and target, including heading levels, list item counts and order, and table dimensions. Fail on any mismatch.

description: Each recurring source term for a device part, procedure or medical concept is translated with the same French term throughout.
verification: Extract recurring source terms and their aligned translations. Fail if any term is rendered with more than one non-synonymous French equivalent, or with variants that could confuse the reader.

description: The deliverable is a valid .srt file that parses without errors (cue number line, timestamp line in HH:MM:SS,mmm --> HH:MM:SS,mmm format, text lines, blank-line separators).
verification: Parse the file with a standard SRT parser; pass if it parses with zero errors and is UTF-8 encoded.

description: The deliverable contains exactly 412 cues, matching the source file.
verification: Count parsed cues in the deliverable and in the source; pass if both equal 412.

description: Every cue number in the deliverable is identical to, and in the same order as, the corresponding source cue number.
verification: Compare the sequence of cue numbers in source and deliverable position by position; pass if all 412 match exactly.

description: Every cue's start and end timestamp is character-for-character identical to the corresponding source cue.
verification: Compare the timestamp line of each cue with the source cue at the same position; pass if all 412 match exactly.

description: No subtitle text line exceeds 42 characters.
verification: Count Unicode characters (code points, including spaces and punctuation, excluding line-ending characters) on every text line; pass if none exceeds 42.

description: No cue contains more than 2 lines of subtitle text.
verification: Count non-empty text lines in each cue; pass if every cue has 1 or 2 lines.

description: Every cue's text is translated into Spanish; no cue is left empty, untranslated, or in English (proper names, brand names, and on-screen terms that are normally kept untranslated are allowed).
verification: Run language identification on each cue's text and compare against the source; pass if no cue is empty, identical to the English source, or detected as English, apart from cues consisting only of names, numbers, or untranslatable terms.

description: Each cue's Spanish text conveys the meaning of the corresponding source cue, without omitted or added content and without content moved to other cues beyond what line-length condensation requires.
verification: Run segment-level translation quality estimation per aligned cue pair; flag cues below threshold, and have a judge review the flagged cues for mistranslation, omission, or addition. Pass if no cue contains a meaning error, omission, or addition that changes what is said. Condensation that drops filler words to fit length limits is allowed.

description: Numbers, quantities, dates, times, and personal or place names in the source appear correctly in the corresponding Spanish cue, using Spanish formatting conventions where these apply.
verification: Extract numbers and named entities from each source cue and check that equivalents appear in the matching target cue. Pass if none is missing or altered in value.

description: The translation uses European (Spain) Spanish conventions rather than Latin American Spanish.
verification: Judge reviews the text for Spain-specific usage: vosotros forms where plural informal address occurs, and Peninsular vocabulary (e.g., 'ordenador', 'coche', 'móvil', not 'computadora', 'carro', 'celular'). Pass if Latin American–specific forms appear in no more than 2 cues.

description: The Spanish text follows standard orthography, including opening ¿ and ¡ marks and correct accents.
verification: Run a Spanish spell and grammar checker. Pass if every interrogative or exclamatory sentence has its opening mark and the checker finds no more than 5 spelling or accent errors across the file.

description: Every sentence of the source email, including the subject line, greeting, and sign-off, is translated, with no source content omitted and no new content added.
verification: Align source and target at the sentence level. Fail if any source sentence has no corresponding target segment, or if any target segment has no source counterpart. Translator notes count as added content unless delivered in a clearly separate file.

description: The translated email is written in French, and no untranslated English sentences remain apart from proper names, product names, and terms that also appear untranslated in the source.
verification: Run language identification on each target sentence. Fail if any sentence is not detected as French, unless it consists only of proper nouns, URLs, or brand names copied from the source.

description: Every number, percentage, currency amount, date, and metric in the source appears in the translation with the identical value and currency.
verification: Extract all numeric values, currency symbols or codes, percentages, and dates from the source and target, then normalize decimal and thousands separators and date formats. Fail if any source value is missing from the target, has a changed value, has a changed currency, or appears in the target with no source counterpart.

description: All names of people, companies, investors, products, and funds are reproduced exactly as in the source.
verification: Extract the proper nouns from the source, using NER plus capitalized tokens, and confirm each appears verbatim in the target. Fail if any is missing, misspelled, or translated.

description: No sentence in the translation changes the meaning of its source sentence, including facts, commitments, asks to investors, positive or negative framing, and hedging.
verification: Run translation quality estimation on each aligned segment pair, and have a bilingual reviewer examine low-scoring segments. Fail if any segment contains a mistranslation that alters a fact, request, tense, negation, or degree of certainty.

description: All URLs, email addresses, and @handles in the source appear unchanged in the translation.
verification: Extract the URLs, email addresses, and handles from both texts. Fail if any source item is missing or altered in the target.

description: The translation keeps the source's paragraph breaks, headings, bullet or numbered lists, and bold or italic emphasis in the same order.
verification: Compare the source and target structure: paragraph count, heading count, list item count per list, and emphasis markers. Fail if any count differs or if elements are reordered.

description: The translation addresses readers with the formal 'vous' form and uses a professional business register, with no slang or texting abbreviations.
verification: Search the target for second-person informal forms (tu, te, toi, ton, ta, tes) used to address the reader, and for slang or abbreviations such as 'stp' or 'mdr'. Fail if any are found.

description: The French reads as natural, grammatically correct business prose, with correct agreement, spelling, accents, and French punctuation spacing.
verification: A judge reads the target and fails it if there are more than 3 grammar, spelling, or accent errors in total, or if any sentence reads as a word-for-word calque that a native French business reader would find unnatural.

description: Every clause, sub-clause, heading, definition, schedule/annex and footnote in the French source has a corresponding English translation, with no source content omitted and no content added.
verification: Segment-align source and target; fail if any source segment lacks a target counterpart or any target segment has no source counterpart (translator notes, if any, must be clearly marked as such and kept separate from the agreement text).

description: The entire agreement text is in English, with no untranslated French passages other than proper names, entity names, addresses, or terms the source itself marks as to be kept in French.
verification: Run language identification per segment; fail if any segment other than the permitted exceptions is detected as French.

description: Every liability cap amount, multiplier, currency, and reference period in the source (e.g., fees paid in the preceding 12 months) appears unchanged in the translation.
verification: Extract all monetary amounts, currencies, multipliers and time periods from the source limitation-of-liability clause(s) and compare with the target; fail on any mismatch, omission, or currency change. Numeric values may be reformatted for English (e.g., 1 000 000,00 € → €1,000,000.00) only if the value stays identical.

description: The limitation-of-liability clause preserves the scope of the cap, its exclusions and carve-outs (e.g., gross negligence/faute lourde, wilful misconduct/dol, excluded damage types), and which party or parties the cap applies to.
verification: Bilingual legal reviewer compares the source and target liability clause(s) and fails if any carve-out, exclusion, damage category, or party allocation is added, dropped, or altered in meaning.

description: The governing law and jurisdiction/dispute resolution clause names the same governing law, the same courts or arbitral body, and the same seat or venue as the source, with no change in meaning.
verification: Compare the source and target governing-law clause(s); fail if the governing law, the named court or tribunal (e.g., Tribunal de commerce de Paris), the city or seat, exclusivity wording, or any arbitration rules differ in meaning.

description: All other numbers, percentages, dates, notice periods, durations, party and entity names, registration numbers, addresses, and clause cross-references match the source.
verification: Extract numbers, dates, named entities and clause references from the source and target and compare; fail on any mismatch. A date format may be converted only if the date is unchanged.

description: Each defined term in the source is rendered by a single English equivalent that is used consistently every time that term appears.
verification: List the source defined terms (capitalized or in the definitions clause), map each to its target rendering, and fail if any term is translated in more than one way across the document.

description: The translation keeps the source's clause numbering, heading hierarchy, ordering, schedules/annexes, and tables.
verification: Compare the source and target section outlines and table counts; fail if numbering, order, or the presence of any section, annex, or table differs.

description: The translation uses formal English contract register and standard common-law contract terminology, with no casual phrasing or contractions.
verification: Judge reads the target and fails on any contraction or slang, or on any phrasing a contract lawyer would consider non-standard or misleading for an English-language agreement.

description: The deliverable contains a translation of every one of the 25 source macros into each of Spanish, German and French (75 translations in total), each traceable to its source macro.
verification: Map each translation to its source macro by ID, title or order. Pass only if all 25 macros have exactly one translation in each of the three languages.

description: Each translation is written entirely in its labeled target language (Spanish, German or French), with no untranslated English sentences left in the body.
verification: Run language identification on every translation and confirm it matches the labeled language. Flag any English sentence remaining in the body. Placeholders, product names and URLs are exempt.

description: Every {{...}} placeholder in a source macro, including {{ticket.requester.first_name}}, appears in each of its translations character-for-character unchanged and the same number of times.
verification: Extract all {{...}} tokens from each source macro and from each translation by regex. Pass only if the token multisets are identical for every source/translation pair. Fail on any translated, re-spaced, re-cased or broken braces.

description: Each translation conveys the full meaning of its source macro, with no sentences or instructions omitted, no content added, and no mistranslations that change what the customer is told or asked to do.
verification: Run sentence alignment and translation quality estimation per source/translation pair. Fail any pair with unaligned source sentences, added sentences, or a meaning-changing error such as a wrong action, negation, condition or time frame.

description: Numbers, URLs, email addresses, phone numbers and product or brand names in the source appear unchanged in every translation.
verification: Extract numbers, URLs, emails, phone numbers and capitalized product or brand names from each source macro. Confirm each appears identically in each translation. Locale-correct decimal separators and date formats are allowed only if the value is unchanged.

description: Each translation keeps the structure of its source macro: the same paragraph breaks, list items and markup (e.g., bold, links, HTML or Markdown).
verification: Compare each source/translation pair on paragraph count, list item count, and the set of markup tags or link elements. Pass if these match for every pair.

description: Within each target language, all 25 macros use one consistent form of addressing the customer (e.g., all tú or all usted; all du or all Sie; all tu or all vous).
verification: Detect second-person pronouns and verb forms in every translation of a language. Pass if no language mixes informal and formal address across or within macros.

description: Translations read as friendly, warm customer support in each language, not stiff or bureaucratic, while staying polite.
verification: A judge reads a sample of at least 5 macros per language and checks three things: natural, warm greetings and closings; empathetic or positive phrasing where the source has it; and no cold legalistic wording, slang or rudeness. Pass if every sampled macro meets this.

description: Every text element of the source birth certificate (headings, field labels, field values, annotations, marginal notes, and stamp/seal text) appears translated in the English deliverable with none omitted.
verification: Align source segments to target segments, including stamp, seal, and margin text. Pass only if every source segment has a corresponding target segment.

description: The translation adds no content absent from the source, other than bracketed translator notes and the translator's certification statement.
verification: Align target to source. Pass only if every target segment, apart from bracketed notes and the certification block, maps to source content.

description: Every personal name in the source (registrant, parents, grandparents, witnesses, officials) is reproduced character-for-character, including accents, ñ, and all surnames, and is not translated or anglicized.
verification: Extract all personal names from the source and check that each appears verbatim (exact string match, including diacritics) in the deliverable. Fail if any name is missing, altered, reordered, or anglicized.

description: Every date in the source (birth, registration, issuance, and any others) appears in the translation with the identical day, month, and year.
verification: Extract every date from the source and target, normalize each to its day, month, and year values, and compare. Fail if any date is missing or any day, month, or year differs, including day/month transposition.

description: All identifying numbers in the source (registry/acta number, book, page, folio, volume, CURP or ID numbers, times of birth) are reproduced identically.
verification: Extract all digit sequences and alphanumeric identifiers from the source and confirm each appears unchanged in the target.

description: Each stamp, seal, and signature on the source document is noted in square brackets at its corresponding position, with a description and a translation of any legible text it contains (e.g., [Seal: Civil Registry of ...]).
verification: Count the stamps, seals, and signatures in the source and the bracketed notes describing them in the target. Pass only if every one has a bracketed note in the matching location and any legible text in it is translated.

description: Apart from proper names and any original-language terms the translator retains in brackets, the deliverable is written in English.
verification: Run language identification on the target text with names excluded. Pass only if all non-name, non-bracketed text is English.

description: The deliverable includes a translator's certification stating that the translation is complete and accurate and that the translator is competent in Spanish and English, with the translator's name, signature line, and date.
verification: Check the deliverable for a certification block containing an accuracy-and-completeness statement, a competence statement, the translator's name, a signature line, and a date.

description: Any source text that cannot be read is marked as [illegible] rather than guessed or silently omitted.
verification: A judge compares the source to the target. Pass if every unreadable portion of the source is marked [illegible] (or similar bracketed wording) and no reconstructed content is presented as if read.

description: The translation follows the source document's structure, presenting sections and fields in the same order and grouping as the original.
verification: A judge compares section and field order between source and target. Pass if the order and grouping match.

description: Every text segment of the source landing page (headline, subheadings, body, buttons/CTAs, captions, footer text) is translated into German, with no segments omitted and no unsupported content added.
verification: Align source and target segments; fail if any source segment has no German counterpart or if the target contains substantive content with no source counterpart.

description: All translated text is in German, with no untranslated English sentences left in, apart from the product name and any terms the buyer has explicitly listed to keep in English.
verification: Run language identification per segment; fail if any segment other than the product name or buyer-listed exempt terms is detected as non-German.

description: The German headline is fewer than 60 characters long, counting spaces and punctuation.
verification: Count the Unicode characters of the main headline (the H1 or the segment the buyer designates as the headline); pass if the count is 59 or fewer.

description: The product name 'FlowDesk' appears exactly as 'FlowDesk' wherever it appears in the source and is never translated, respelled, or changed in capitalization.
verification: Count occurrences of 'FlowDesk' in source and target; fail if the target count is lower than the source count, or if variants like 'Flowdesk', 'Flow Desk', or translated forms appear.

description: All numbers, prices, percentages, dates, URLs, email addresses, and other proper names in the source appear unchanged in meaning in the German text, with German number and date formatting allowed.
verification: Extract these entities from source and target and compare them after normalizing locale formats (for example 1,000.50 → 1.000,50); fail on any missing or altered value.

description: The German text conveys the same claims, offers, and calls to action as the source, with no mistranslations that change the meaning.
verification: A bilingual quality-estimation check plus judge review of aligned segments; fail if any segment changes, omits, or inverts a claim, offer, or CTA.

description: The German reads as natural, grammatical marketing copy, with no literal word-for-word phrasing that a native reader would find awkward, and with consistent use of either 'Sie' or 'du' throughout.
verification: A judge reads the target and fails it on grammar or spelling errors, clearly unidiomatic calques, or mixing of Sie and du forms.

description: The deliverable keeps the source's structure and format: the same file type, the same order of sections and headings, and markup or placeholders (HTML tags, variables, links) left intact.
verification: Compare source and target structure: the same heading and section sequence, the same set of tags or placeholders, and link targets unchanged; fail on any break or loss.

description: Every source segment of the purchase order, including headers, addresses, terms, notes, and all line items, appears translated in the Spanish deliverable, and no content is added or omitted.
verification: Segment-align source and target. Pass if every source segment has a corresponding Spanish segment and no target segment lacks a source counterpart. Untranslatable items (SKUs, codes, proper names) count as covered when they are carried over.

description: The translated purchase order contains exactly the same number of line items, in the same order, as the source.
verification: Count line items (table rows or item entries) in source and target and compare their order. Pass only if the counts are equal and the order is identical.

description: Every SKU/item code in the source appears character-for-character identical in the corresponding line item of the translation.
verification: Extract all SKUs from the source line items and do an exact string match against the same line item in the target. Fail on any missing, altered, or reordered SKU.

description: Every quantity in each line item has the same numeric value as in the source, and the unit of measure is the same or correctly translated.
verification: Extract the quantity for each line item in source and target and compare the numeric values after normalizing the decimal separator. Fail on any value mismatch. Confirm that units are equivalent.

description: Every price and amount (unit prices, line totals, subtotal, tax, shipping, grand total) has the same numeric value and currency as in the source.
verification: Extract every monetary amount and currency from source and target, then compare them pairwise after normalizing the decimal and thousands separators. Fail on any value or currency mismatch, or any missing amount.

description: PO number, dates, company and person names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, and tax IDs are preserved without alteration (dates may be reformatted only if the calendar date is unchanged).
verification: Extract these entities from the source and check that each appears in the target. Pass if names, codes, and contact details match exactly and every date resolves to the same calendar date.

description: All translatable text in the deliverable is in Spanish, with no untranslated English sentences or labels remaining.
verification: Run language identification per segment. Pass if every translatable segment is identified as Spanish. Segments made up only of SKUs, codes, numbers, or proper names are exempt.

description: The Spanish text accurately conveys the meaning of the source, including item descriptions and commercial terms (payment terms, delivery terms, Incoterms), without mistranslations that change obligations.
verification: Run a quality-estimation pass per segment, plus a judge review of the terms and item descriptions. Fail if any segment's meaning is changed, for example a wrong item description, altered payment or delivery terms, or a negation error.

description: The deliverable keeps the source document's layout structure: the same sections, a line-item table with the same columns, and totals in the same positions.
verification: Compare the section headings, table column count, and the positions of the totals block between source and target. Pass if the structure corresponds one-to-one.

description: The deliverable contains exactly five localized emails, one for each of the five source onboarding emails, each clearly matched to its source email.
verification: Count the localized emails and confirm a one-to-one mapping to the five source emails by order, filename, or label. Pass only if all five are present and none is duplicated or missing.

description: Every source segment in each email, including subject line, preheader, body, buttons/CTAs, and footer, is translated into French with nothing omitted and no content added.
verification: Align source and target segments per email. Fail if any source segment has no target counterpart, is left in English (except brand/product names), or if the target contains substantive content with no source counterpart.

description: All translated text is in French as used in France (fr-FR), not Canadian or other regional French.
verification: Run language identification on every target segment, which must be French. Then have a fr-FR reviewer or verifier check for Québécois-specific vocabulary or spelling (e.g. 'courriel' is acceptable, but 'magasiner' or 'char' fail). Fail if any segment is non-French or uses clearly non-France regional usage.

description: Every date in the source appears in the target in DD/MM/YYYY numeric format and represents the same calendar date as the source.
verification: Extract all dates from source and target. Check that each target date matches the regex ^\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}$ and that day, month and year equal those of the corresponding source date (e.g. 03/04/2025 source in US format becomes 04/03/2025). Fail on any wrong format, swapped day/month, or missing date.

description: Every monetary amount is expressed in euros using French formatting, with the € symbol after the number separated by a space (e.g. '49,90 €'), and no other currency symbols or codes remain.
verification: Extract all monetary amounts from the target. Pass only if each uses the € symbol placed after the number with a space (regular or non-breaking), uses a comma as the decimal separator where decimals appear, and no '$', '£', 'USD', or a leading '€' appears.

description: Each monetary amount has the numeric value agreed for the euro version: either the source number unchanged, or a conversion at the agreed rate, per the buyer's answer to the open question.
verification: Pair each source amount with its target amount. Check that the target value equals the source value, or the source value times the agreed rate rounded to 2 decimals, depending on the agreed rule. Fail on any mismatch or any amount that is dropped.

description: All merge tags/placeholders (e.g. {{first_name}}, %NAME%), URLs, email addresses, and HTML tags from the source are preserved unchanged in the target.
verification: Extract placeholders, URLs, email addresses and HTML tags from each source email and its target. Pass only if the multisets match exactly, with none altered, translated, added or removed.

description: Each localized email keeps the source's structure: the same order of sections, paragraphs, lists, headings, bold/links emphasis, and file format.
verification: Compare source and target per email for section/paragraph count and order, list items, headings and markup, and confirm the file format matches the source. Fail on missing, merged or reordered structural elements.

description: The French reads as natural, idiomatic marketing/onboarding copy for France, with a single consistent form of address (vous or tu) across all five emails and correct grammar and spelling.
verification: A judge reads all five emails. Fail if it finds literal calques that a native fr-FR reader would find unnatural, any mixing of vous and tu, or grammar or spelling errors (including missing French spacing before ? ! : ;). Note each issue found.

description: The abstract and all 14 claims are fully translated, with every source sentence and clause rendered and no content added that is absent from the source.
verification: Align source and target at the sentence and clause level. Fail if any source segment has no corresponding target segment, or if any target segment has no source counterpart.

description: The translation contains exactly claims 1 through 14, numbered identically to the source, with each numbered claim translating the same-numbered source claim.
verification: Extract claim numbers from source and target. Pass only if both sequences are exactly 1-14 with no gaps, duplicates or renumbering, and alignment maps each source claim N to target claim N.

description: Every dependent claim refers to exactly the same claim number(s) as in the source (e.g., 'nach Anspruch 3' becomes 'according to claim 3'), and independent claims remain independent.
verification: Parse each claim's back-references in source and target (patterns such as 'nach/gemäß Anspruch N', 'nach einem der Ansprüche N bis M' and their English equivalents). Fail if any claim's set of referenced claim numbers or ranges differs, or if an independent claim gains or loses a reference.

description: All numbers, numeric ranges, units, chemical formulas and parenthetical reference signs in the source appear unchanged in the corresponding target segment.
verification: Extract numeric tokens, units, formulas and parenthesized reference numerals per aligned segment. Normalize decimal commas to points (e.g., '2,5' to '2.5'). Fail on any missing, altered or extra value.

description: No translated segment changes the technical meaning or claim scope of the source, for example by mistranslating a feature, dropping a limitation, or changing 'mindestens'/'höchstens', 'oder'/'und' or a negation.
verification: A translation quality-estimation verifier compares aligned segments and flags meaning errors. Fail if any segment contains a major accuracy error that alters a technical feature, logical connector, quantifier or limitation.

description: Each recurring German technical term is translated with the same English term throughout the abstract and claims.
verification: Build a term list of German nouns and noun phrases occurring two or more times and check their aligned English renderings. Fail if any term is rendered with different English terms in different places, unless the source itself varies.

description: Indefinite and definite articles in the claims mirror the source's antecedent structure: a feature introduced with 'ein/eine' is introduced with 'a/an', and later references using 'der/die/das' or 'dieser' use 'the' or 'said'.
verification: The judge reviews each claim and fails the criterion if any feature is introduced with a definite article in English where the source uses an indefinite one, or vice versa, at first mention or subsequent mention.

description: The deliverable is in English, with no untranslated German words or sentences except proper names, trade names and reference signs.
verification: Run language identification per sentence and a German-word scan against a dictionary. Fail if any sentence is identified as German or contains untranslated German common words.

description: The abstract is kept as a separate, labeled section, distinct from the claims, and each claim remains a single sentence ending in a period, as in the source.
verification: Check that a section labeled 'Abstract' exists and is separate from the claims. Count sentence-terminal periods per claim and fail if any claim is split into multiple sentences where the source has one.

description: Every source segment of the Spanish judgment (headings, body, footnotes, operative part, signatures and stamps text) has a corresponding English translation, with no segments omitted.
verification: Align source and target segments; fail if any source segment containing text has no aligned target segment or if the translation stops before the end of the source.

description: The translation adds no content absent from the source, such as commentary, summaries or explanatory notes, except clearly marked translator's notes.
verification: Segment alignment flags target segments with no source counterpart; fail if any unaligned content is found that is not explicitly labelled as a translator's note.

description: The translation is written entirely in English, with Spanish retained only for proper names, case numbers, statute titles or terms the translator explicitly glosses.
verification: Run language identification per segment; fail if any segment is detected as Spanish, excluding proper names, case/reference numbers and glossed legal terms.

description: All numbers, monetary amounts, dates, case and docket numbers, article and statute references, and time limits match the source exactly in value.
verification: Extract all numerals, amounts, dates (normalising format, e.g. '3 de marzo de 2023' = 'March 3, 2023' or '3 March 2023') and statutory references from source and target; fail on any missing or differing value.

description: All names of parties, judges, lawyers, courts and places from the source appear in the translation, spelled as in the source.
verification: Extract named entities from the source and check each appears in the target with identical spelling (accents may be retained); fail on any missing or altered name.

description: The operative part of the judgment (the 'fallo'/decision: who wins, what is ordered, dismissed or upheld, costs awarded, and appeal rights) is translated with its legal meaning unchanged.
verification: Judge compares the source 'FALLO' (or equivalent decision section) with its translation and fails if any outcome, order, party obligation, costs ruling or appeal deadline is reversed, omitted or materially changed.

description: The translation as a whole conveys the meaning of the source accurately, without mistranslations that change facts, legal reasoning or holdings.
verification: Run translation quality estimation on aligned segments and have a judge review flagged low-scoring segments; fail if any segment contains a mistranslation that alters a fact, legal argument or conclusion.

description: The translation uses formal legal English consistent with court documents: no contractions, slang or colloquial phrasing, and consistent rendering of recurring legal terms.
verification: Check for contractions and colloquialisms deterministically; judge confirms each recurring legal term (e.g. 'demandante', 'recurso', 'sentencia') is rendered consistently throughout.

description: The translation preserves the source's structure: section headings (e.g. Antecedentes de Hecho, Fundamentos de Derecho, Fallo), paragraph and numbering order.
verification: Compare heading count, numbered paragraph sequence and section order between source and target; fail if any heading or numbered item is missing, merged or reordered.

description: The deliverable's module and test file import without error under Python 3.12.
verification: In a clean Python 3.12 sandbox with only pytest installed, import the parser module and run `pytest --collect-only`. Pass if both complete with no import or syntax errors.

description: The parser code imports only Python standard-library modules; the test code may additionally import pytest.
verification: Parse all import statements in the delivered .py files and compare them against sys.stdlib_module_names for Python 3.12. Allow pytest only in test files. Pass if there are no other imports and no third-party packages appear in any requirements or config file.

description: Calling the parser function with 'P3DT4H' returns 273600 total seconds.
verification: Call the parser function in the sandbox with 'P3DT4H'. Pass if the result is numerically equal to 273600.

description: The function correctly converts the day, hour, minute and second components, alone and combined, to total seconds.
verification: Run the reference cases: 'PT1H'=3600, 'PT30M'=1800, 'PT45S'=45, 'P1D'=86400, 'P1DT1H1M1S'=90061, 'P2DT30M'=174600, 'PT0S'=0. Pass only if every result is numerically equal to the expected value.

description: The function supports the ISO 8601 week form, so 'P2W' returns 1209600.
verification: Call the function with 'P2W'. Pass if the result is numerically equal to 1209600.

description: The function raises an exception, rather than returning a value, for malformed duration strings.
verification: Call the function with each of: '', 'P', 'PT', '3DT4H', 'P1H', 'PT4D', 'abc', 'P3DT'. Pass only if every call raises an exception.

description: A pytest test file is included and all of its tests pass under Python 3.12.
verification: Run `pytest` in the sandbox on the delivered tests. Pass if at least one test is collected, the exit code is 0, and there are no failures, errors or skips.

description: The tests include at least 5 test cases, covering at least one combined date-and-time duration, at least one single-component duration, and at least one invalid input that is expected to raise.
verification: Count the test cases collected by pytest, with parametrized cases counted individually; pass requires 5 or more. Then inspect the test inputs: pass only if they include a duration with both a day part and a T time part, a duration with exactly one component, and a malformed string asserted with pytest.raises.

description: The deliverable contains only the parser function, any helpers it needs, and its tests, with no unrelated code or files.
verification: List the delivered files and top-level definitions. Fail if there are files or functions unrelated to parsing ISO 8601 durations or testing that parser, such as unrelated scripts, a web app, or a CLI that was not requested.

description: The modified project installs and starts without errors using the repository's existing install and start/build commands.
verification: In a sandbox, run the repo's install command and build/start script (or lint/typecheck if defined); pass if all exit successfully with no errors.

description: All tests that existed before the change still pass, and none were deleted, skipped, or weakened to make them pass.
verification: Run the full test suite in a sandbox; pass if every pre-existing test passes and a diff shows no pre-existing test removed, marked skip/only, or had its assertions altered except where the response shape for GET /orders necessarily changed.

description: New automated tests cover default page size, max page size limit, cursor traversal to the next page, and the last page, and all of them pass.
verification: Inspect the diff for new test cases covering each of the four behaviours; run the suite and confirm they pass. Fail if any of the four is untested or any new test fails.

description: GET /orders with no page-size parameter returns at most 20 orders.
verification: Seed more than 20 orders, call GET /orders without a limit parameter, and assert exactly 20 items are returned.

description: Requests asking for more than 100 items never return more than 100 orders.
verification: Seed more than 100 orders, request a limit of 500; pass if the response either contains at most 100 items or is a 4xx validation error, and never more than 100 items.

description: Following the returned cursor from the first page to the last returns every order exactly once with no duplicates or gaps.
verification: Seed N orders (e.g., 57), page through using the returned next cursor with a limit of 20 until no next cursor is returned; pass if the collected IDs equal the full seeded set with no duplicates, in a consistent order.

description: Pagination uses an opaque or key-based cursor rather than page-number/offset parameters.
verification: Read the handler and query code; pass if the next page is selected by a cursor value (e.g., last-seen ID/timestamp) rather than skip/offset/page number arithmetic.

description: The final page's response clearly indicates there are no more results (for example, a null or absent next cursor).
verification: Request the last page; pass if the next-cursor field is null/absent (or a hasMore flag is false) and a subsequent request is not suggested.

description: A malformed cursor value yields a 4xx client error rather than a 500 or crash.
verification: Call GET /orders with cursor=garbage!!; pass if the status code is in the 400-499 range.

description: Changes are limited to the GET /orders pagination feature and its tests, with no unrelated refactors or dependency changes.
verification: Review the diff; pass if all modified files relate to the /orders route, its data access, or tests, and no unrelated endpoints or package dependencies are changed without justification.

description: The project builds with the repo's existing build command without new errors after the change.
verification: Run the repo's install and build scripts (e.g., npm ci && npm run build) in a sandbox; pass if exit code is 0 and no new compile/type errors appear compared to the base commit.

description: Selecting or displaying a date in the date picker shows the intended calendar day when the runtime timezone is UTC-negative (e.g., America/Los_Angeles, America/New_York, Pacific/Honolulu).
verification: Run the date picker tests (including the new regression test) with TZ set to America/Los_Angeles, America/New_York, and Pacific/Honolulu; pass if a date chosen/passed as YYYY-MM-DD renders and returns that same day in every timezone.

description: The fix does not break correct day display in UTC and UTC-positive timezones.
verification: Run the same date picker tests with TZ=UTC and TZ=Asia/Tokyo and TZ=Pacific/Auckland; pass if all show and return the intended calendar day.

description: A new automated test is added that reproduces the UTC-negative wrong-day bug using the repo's existing test framework.
verification: Inspect the diff for at least one new test case targeting the date picker that sets or mocks a UTC-negative timezone; run it against the original (unfixed) code and confirm it fails, then against the fixed code and confirm it passes.

description: All tests that passed on the base commit still pass after the change.
verification: Run the repo's full test command on the base commit and on the delivered commit; pass if no test that passed before fails after.

description: Changes are limited to the date picker fix, its regression test, and directly required supporting code; no unrelated refactors or feature changes.
verification: Review the diff; pass if every modified file and hunk relates to date/timezone handling for the date picker or its tests (dependency additions only if needed for the fix and justified).

description: No new runtime dependencies are added unless the deliverable explains why the fix requires them.
verification: Compare package.json dependencies between base and delivered commit; pass if none added, or if any addition is accompanied by a written justification in the PR/notes.

description: The deliverable includes a short written explanation of the root cause and how the fix addresses it.
verification: Check the PR description, commit message, or notes file for an explanation naming the cause (e.g., parsing a date-only string as UTC midnight then rendering in local time) and the fix approach.

description: The project is written in Go and builds without errors using `go build` on the module root (or the main package path documented in the README).
verification: In a clean sandbox with a current stable Go toolchain, run `go build ./...` (after `go mod download` if a go.mod exists); pass if exit code is 0 and source files are .go.

description: The CLI accepts a path to a CSV file as input (as documented in the README) and writes output to standard output.
verification: Run the built binary with a sample CSV file path using the invocation shown in the README; pass if it exits 0 and prints non-empty output to stdout.

description: Output is JSON Lines: exactly one valid JSON object per CSV data row, one per line, in the same order as the input rows, with no header row emitted as data.
verification: For a test CSV with a header and N data rows, check stdout has exactly N non-empty lines, each parses as a JSON object, and line i corresponds to data row i.

description: The first CSV row is treated as headers, and each output object uses those header names as keys mapped to the corresponding field values of that row.
verification: With input `name,age\nAlice,30\nBob,25`, pass if output objects are {"name":"Alice","age":"30"} and {"name":"Bob","age":"25"} (keys exact; values compared as their string content, numeric typing accepted if values are equal).

description: Quoted CSV fields are parsed per RFC 4180: commas inside quotes, escaped double quotes (""), and newlines inside quotes are preserved as part of a single field value.
verification: Feed a CSV row such as `"Smith, John","He said ""hi""","line1\nline2"` under a 3-column header; pass if the output object has exactly 3 keys with values `Smith, John`, `He said "hi"`, and `line1\nline2` (embedded newline), and remains one JSON line.

description: Field values containing characters that require JSON escaping (quotes, backslashes, newlines, non-ASCII UTF-8) are emitted as valid JSON that round-trips to the original value.
verification: Run a CSV containing backslashes, double quotes, embedded newlines, and UTF-8 text (e.g., `café`); parse each output line and compare values to the source strings exactly.

description: The CLI exits with a non-zero status and an error message on stderr when the input file does not exist or the CSV is malformed (e.g., an unterminated quote).
verification: Run with a nonexistent path and with a file containing an unterminated quoted field; pass if both runs exit non-zero and write a message to stderr.

description: The deliverable includes a README file that explains how to build the tool and gives at least one usage example showing the command invocation and sample input/output.
verification: Check for a README (README.md or README) at the repository root containing build instructions, a command-line invocation example, and an example of CSV input with the resulting JSON lines; pass if the documented invocation actually runs as described.

description: All dependencies are either the Go standard library or declared in a go.mod/go.sum so the build is reproducible.
verification: Inspect imports; pass if every non-stdlib import is listed in go.mod and `go build` succeeds without manual dependency steps beyond those in the README.

description: The deliverable is provided as a pull request or patch against the buyer's website repository that applies cleanly to the agreed base commit.
verification: Apply the patch or PR to the agreed base commit and confirm it applies without conflicts.

description: The modified site builds with the project's existing build command without errors.
verification: Run the project's documented build command in a clean sandbox on the patched code and confirm it exits with status 0.

description: On each agreed page, the median Lighthouse Performance score (mobile preset, 5 runs) after the change is at least 10 points above the baseline or is at least 90.
verification: Run Lighthouse 5 times per page on the base commit and on the patched build under identical conditions, take the median score, and compare it per page; every page must meet the threshold.

description: On each agreed page, the median Largest Contentful Paint after the change is at least 20% lower than the baseline median.
verification: From the same 5-run Lighthouse measurements, compare the median LCP for each page before and after; every page must show a reduction of at least 20%.

description: All automated tests that passed on the base commit still pass after the change.
verification: Run the existing test suite in a sandbox on the base commit and on the patched code; no test that passed before may fail after.

description: Speed gains do not come from removing or hiding page content, features, or functionality. All visible text, images, links, and forms on the agreed pages remain present and working.
verification: Render each agreed page before and after and compare visible text, image count, links, and form elements. Submit each form and click each navigation link to confirm they still work. The criterion fails if anything was removed or broken without the buyer's approval.

description: Each agreed page looks the same as before the change at mobile (375px) and desktop (1366px) widths.
verification: Capture full-page screenshots before and after at both widths and run a pixel diff. Any region differing by more than 1% of the page area must be reviewed by a judge, who fails the criterion if the layout, styling, or imagery has visibly changed.

description: The deliverable includes a report listing, for each agreed page, the baseline and after values for the Lighthouse Performance score and LCP, the measurement method, and each change made with the files it touched.
verification: Confirm the report exists and contains before/after values for both metrics on every agreed page, a method description, and a list of changes that maps to the diff.

description: The deliverable includes a workflow file under .github/workflows/ with a .yml or .yaml extension that is valid YAML and passes actionlint with no errors.
verification: Check that the file path matches .github/workflows/*.y{a,}ml. Parse it as YAML, then run actionlint on it. Fail on any parse error or any actionlint error.

description: The workflow is triggered by the pull_request event without branch or path filters that would exclude PRs to the default branch.
verification: Parse the 'on' key and confirm pull_request is present. If branches, branches-ignore, paths or paths-ignore filters exist, confirm they do not exclude PRs targeting the default branch for ordinary code changes.

description: Every job that runs lint, typecheck or tests sets up Node.js major version 24.
verification: In each relevant job, find actions/setup-node and confirm node-version resolves to major 24 (e.g., '24', '24.x', or an .nvmrc/.node-version file containing 24). Fail if any such job uses another version or omits setup-node.

description: The workflow installs pnpm and installs workspace dependencies with pnpm before running lint, typecheck or tests.
verification: Confirm that pnpm is installed (pnpm/action-setup or corepack enable) and that a 'pnpm install' step runs before the lint, typecheck and test steps in each job that runs them.

description: The workflow caches the pnpm store, with a cache key tied to pnpm-lock.yaml.
verification: Pass if either (a) actions/setup-node sets cache: pnpm, or (b) actions/cache caches the pnpm store path (from 'pnpm store path' or an equivalent explicit path) with a key that includes hashFiles of pnpm-lock.yaml. Fail otherwise.

description: The workflow has a step that runs the repository's lint across the monorepo through pnpm.
verification: Find a step whose run command invokes lint via pnpm, for example 'pnpm lint', 'pnpm run lint', 'pnpm -r lint', or 'pnpm turbo lint'.

description: The workflow has a step that runs type checking across the monorepo through pnpm.
verification: Find a step whose run command invokes typecheck via pnpm, for example 'pnpm typecheck', 'pnpm -r typecheck', or 'pnpm exec tsc --noEmit'.

description: The workflow has a step that runs the test suite across the monorepo through pnpm.
verification: Find a step whose run command invokes tests via pnpm, for example 'pnpm test', 'pnpm -r test', or 'pnpm turbo test'.

description: A failure in lint, typecheck or tests makes the workflow run fail.
verification: Confirm that no lint, typecheck or test step, and no job containing one, sets continue-on-error: true. Confirm that none of those run commands mask the exit code (for example with '|| true' or '; exit 0').

description: On a fixture pnpm monorepo, the workflow succeeds when all checks pass and fails when any one check fails.
verification: Use act or an equivalent runner on a fixture pnpm workspace that has root lint, typecheck and test scripts and simulate a pull_request event. The run must succeed when all scripts pass. In three further runs, make the lint, typecheck and test scripts fail one at a time; each of those runs must fail.

description: The deliverable changes only CI workflow files under .github/ and does not modify application code, package.json or the lockfile.
verification: Diff the deliverable against the base and confirm that every changed or added file is under .github/.

description: The up migration runs without error on a Postgres database containing an existing users table with an email column.
verification: In a sandbox Postgres instance, create users (buyer-provided schema, or a minimal table with id and email columns plus sample rows), run the up migration, and confirm it exits with no errors.

description: After the up migration, users has a nullable column named deleted_at of a timestamp type (timestamp or timestamptz) with no default value.
verification: Query information_schema.columns for users.deleted_at. Confirm data_type is 'timestamp without time zone' or 'timestamp with time zone', is_nullable = 'YES', and column_default IS NULL.

description: The migration does not write any values to existing rows: deleted_at is NULL for every pre-existing row and no other column values change.
